thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 P1 — Region fallback loop detected. Health checks flapping across regions (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). Multiple model swaps and rising 5xx/timeout rate. Automatic fallback triggered repeatedly.

sre_oncall_jamie: acked. paging @pagerduty. oncall taking.

pagerduty: Paging oncall: @sre_oncall_jamie — incident acknowledged.

alice: seeing repeated model variant swaps in the routing logs. Any chance a bad variant landed in us-west?

mike: checking now. early signal: us-west health checks showing OOMs on model-worker pods after a recent flavor rollout at ~2765432000. That causes fallback to us-east, which then pushes traffic and makes eu probes time out. looks like a cascade.

carla: if us-west worker OOMs -> service reports unhealthy -> smart-router routes to next region -> next region gets overloaded -> its health probes degrade -> routing bounces back. classic baton-passing healthflip.

sre_oncall_jamie: impact? are customer-facing APIs failing or just internal routing churn?

support-ops: customer-facing. Hosted API errors up ~6% for the last 5m, p50 latency +120ms, and several customers opened tickets. 4 paid customers reported timeouts. No major data loss.

alice: can we stop the automatic fallback first so it doesn't keep hopping? I want to pin a destination while we heal us-west.

mike: agree. temp mitigation: disable auto-fallback and pin traffic to us-east primary for the orgs with incidents. Doing via control-plane.

carla: runbook step — disable fallback for the cluster scope and increase probe debounce. Example:
```bash
# set sticky routing to primary for the org
curl -s -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"scope":"org:org_12","override":{"policy":"sticky_primary","ttl":"30s","fallback":false}}'
```

runtime-eng: applying pin for org_12 -> routing policy now sticky to us-east. patch id: rp-9382.

runtime-eng: also found a bad variant rollout in us-west: model "gpt-open-cpu-int8" was pushed by canary job and it causes sporadic worker OOMs under our typical request mix. rolling it back to "gpt-open-quant-v2" now.

mike: rollback command used: `redwoodctl model pin --region us-west --model gpt-open-quant-v2 --force`

incident-bot: automated check: model variant in us-west is now gpt-open-quant-v2 (confirmed). Health checks re-evaluating.

carla: additionally increase healthcheck success threshold and probe interval to reduce flipflop while nodes stabilize: set probe.window = 5, probe.interval=10s.

runtime-eng: applied probe debounce changes cluster-wide for routing groups affected. patch id: probe-441.

support-ops: customer-facing errors dropping to ~1.1% after the pin. latency trending back to normal. Two customers still reporting intermittent 504s, routing logs show them hitting eu briefly before being routed back.

alice: I'll keep sticky override for 20m then gradually re-enable fallback with a higher backoff. plan: re-enable with backoff multiplier x3 and circuit open for 5m after a fail.

mike: +1. commands to re-enable later: `curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/routing/overrides -d '{"scope":"org:org_12","override":{"policy":"smart","fallback":true,"backoff_multiplier":3}}'`

runtime-eng: monitoring KV cache and worker memory usage. no further OOMs observed in us-west since rollback.

support-ops: tally of customer impact: ~30 orgs saw transient 5xx, 4 support escalations (one marked SEV), no SLA credits yet but tracking.

sre_oncall_jamie: good mitigation. next steps: 1) keep sticky override for 20m, 2) run a controlled canary of the variant in us-west on reduced qps, 3) create postmortem template. I'll hand back to oncall after we hit 30m of stable metrics.

carla: note for postmortem — root cause is twofold: variant rollout with insufficient resource profile for typical workload + too-aggressive routing fallback thresholds (low debounce) which allowed region-to-region baton passing.

alice: filing postmortem doc now and adding checklist: model-variant-resource-tests, routing fallback hysteresis, probe debounce defaults.

incident-bot: SUMMARY — mitigations applied: pinned routing to us-east for affected orgs (rp-9382), rolled back bad variant in us-west to gpt-open-quant-v2, increased probe debounce (probe-441). Customer impact: transient 5xxs for ~30 orgs, 4 escalations.

support-ops: adding affected customer IDs to the incident tracker. will coordinate comms.

sre_oncall_jamie: handing incident to routine monitoring. reopening if flip starts again. thanks all. :thumbsup: :medal: 

runtime-eng: leaving a follow-up task to add variant resource validation in CI.

alice: postmortem draft created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2765432100 (will link final after review).

incident-bot: incident closed to on-call; flagged for postmortem.
